providers.name: TonMobile
providers.tag: Lowest price per day for one-country trips
providers.best_for: City breaks and one- to two-week stays in a single country
facts: 1 GB a day on unlimited plans
providers.summary: TonMobile lists seven-day unlimited plans at $16.50 for France and the UK and $17.70 for Spain, Germany, Portugal, Greece and the Netherlands (October 2026). Buying needs no documents, and cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and crypto are accepted. The Europe plan covers 35 countries but has fixed data, not unlimited.
pros: Lowest price per day for single-country unlimited plans
Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay and crypto payments
cons: Only 1 GB of full-speed data per day
No regional unlimited plan for Europe
Data-only, no phone number

providers.name: Ubigi
providers.tag: Large fair-use allowance on one Europe plan
providers.best_for: Longer multi-country trips with a lot of data
facts: 25 GB fair use, then a reduced speed
providers.summary: Ubigi lists a Europe Unlimited plan for 7, 15 and 30 days across 38 destinations, including the UK, Switzerland and Norway. On the 7-day plan page a fair use limit of 25 GB applies, after which the speed is reduced. It accepts many card types, Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal.
pros: Large full-speed allowance on the plan page
cons: Fair use limit rather than a daily number
Whether an ID check applies was not found in our sources

providers.name: Airalo
providers.tag: Widest country list among the big names
providers.best_for: Border-hopping routes with less common destinations
providers.summary: Airalo lists two unlimited tiers for Europe: Eurolink with 41 countries and 5 GB a day, and a cheaper EUconnect with 28 countries and a 3 GB cap. Weekly Eurolink pricing is close to Saily's according to eSIMDB.
cons: No price advantage over Saily
Cheaper tier covers fewer non-EU countries

providers.name: Saily
providers.tag: Regional unlimited for heavy daily use
providers.best_for: Multi-country routes with lots of mobile streaming
providers.summary: Saily sells one Europe unlimited eSIM for 35 countries with a 5 GB daily allowance. According to eSIMDB, a week costs $28.99 and 30 days $71.99, so it makes most sense for long trips that change country often.
cons: Roughly 75% more than TonMobile for a seven-day trip
Data-only

providers.name: GigSky
providers.tag: 43-country plan with trial and tiered fixed packs
providers.best_for: Travellers who want to try a small plan first
providers.summary: GigSky's own blog describes a Europe eSIM for 43 countries including the UK and Turkey. Its unlimited plans are priced by duration and drop in speed after 3.5 GB of high-speed data a day. Tethering is supported, and a free 500 MB trial is mentioned.
cons: Final prices are shown in the app and vary
Payment methods were not found in our sources

providers.name: Maya Mobile
providers.tag: 5 GB a day with hotspot on all plans
providers.summary: According to eSIMDB, Maya Mobile's Europe plan gives 5 GB a day at full speed and allows hotspot on all plans. Sources disagree on the country count, from 36 to 49, so check the list for your route.
cons: Sources disagree on the country list
Official pages were hard to verify

providers.name: Jetpac
providers.tag: Many lengths and unlimited hotspot, per its own blog
providers.best_for: Short and mid-length trips that need flexible durations
providers.summary: Jetpac lists Europe unlimited plans from 3 to 30 days according to eSIMDB, with 3 GB a day at full speed. Its own blog says unlimited hotspot is included on unlimited plans. Country counts differ between sources.
pros: Hotspot included according to its blog
cons: Conflicting prices and country counts between sources
Payment methods were not found

providers.name: Nomad
providers.tag: Short unlimited trips and a cheap large fixed plan
providers.best_for: Five- to ten-day trips, or travellers under 1.5 GB a day
providers.summary: Nomad lists unlimited Europe plans for 35 countries with 2 GB a day, but only for 5 or 10 days. Its stronger offer, according to eSIMDB, is a fixed 50 GB plan for 30 days.
pros: Large fixed plan at a low price
cons: No unlimited plan longer than 10 days
Mid-range daily allowance

providers.name: Yesim
providers.tag: No ID check and cheap fixed plans
providers.best_for: Travellers with modest data needs who prefer fixed plans
providers.summary: Yesim sells a Europe and UK eSIM for 33 countries, with fixed and unlimited tabs. Its page mentions a fair usage policy that may throttle after a daily limit, without giving the number. It states no ID is required and unused plans are refundable within 30 days.
cons: Daily limit on unlimited not published
Hotspot rule unclear for Europe

providers.name: Holafly
providers.tag: No published daily cap on phone data
providers.best_for: Travellers who want no fixed daily number for phone use
facts: Fair use policy, no daily cap listed
providers.summary: Holafly relies on a fair use policy instead of a published daily cap, and covers 33 countries in Europe. Adam and Linds report hotspot sharing limited to about 1 GB a day on prepaid plans (August 2026).
pros: No published daily cap for phone use
cons: Fair use slowdowns are not quantified
Tight hotspot limit
Highest 30-day price among the five providers with listed prices

providers.name: Flexiroam
providers.tag: Fixed-data Europe packs with a required app
providers.best_for: Travellers who want a large fixed pack for a short trip
facts: Fixed packs seen up to 100 GB
Unlimited tab on its Europe page
providers.summary: Flexiroam's Europe page lists fixed packs such as 10 GB for 3 days and 100 GB for 15 days, plus an Unlimited tab. We could not confirm the unlimited details, the country list or the hotspot rule, so its scores are conservative.
pros: Large fixed packs for short trips
cons: Unlimited details not confirmed in our sources
Hotspot rule not confirmed
